Resolves #18731

🌿 Deferred work now asks whether its window still exists at the moment it resumes, instead of trusting an answer given 50ms earlier to a different question.

**The ticket's own hypothesis was wrong, and measuring is what retired it.** #18731 proposed a stale `outerRect` after a resize-without-move, with `#18068` as precedent. The three arms never reach a geometry assertion at all — they die at `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:138`, the shared whitebox check that no worker error reached the page console. `the target is substantially wider`, the symptom the ticket records, appears **zero** times in every run below.

## Two causes, separated by measurement

| cause | discharged by |
|---|---|
| 21 duplicate `Observable` registrations from `tab.plugin.Overflow` | #18748 / #18749 — measured 21 → 0, already on `dev` |
| remote calls issued into a window that has already departed | **this PR** |

## The second cause is a leak, not a race — and that decided the fix

I instrumented `isWindowDeparted()` on both sides of the `await` in `addResizeObserver` and ran the whole file:

```
304 addResizeObserver calls
 295  departedBeforeAwait=false  departedAfterAwait=false
   9  departedBeforeAwait=true   departedAfterAwait=true
   0  departedBeforeAwait=false  departedAfterAwait=true   ← the in-flight race I had predicted
```

**Zero races.** The nine match the nine dead-port errors one-for-one, three per window across three windows, and both components reported `mounted === true` while their window was gone. So the call was never losing a race; it should never have started.

`updateDomListeners()` gates its deferred mount on `component.mounted` when it **schedules**, 50ms before the work runs. `mixin.DomEvents#initDomEvents` defers 150ms and checks nothing at all. `mounted` cannot bridge either gap: the App Worker's component model outlives its window's port.

**The check therefore sits in `mountDomListeners()`** — the single point both schedulers funnel through — rather than at each scheduler. A third scheduler inherits it instead of having to remember it. My first attempt guarded the 50ms call site only; the e2e then showed 4 of 9 errors surviving, which is how the 150ms path was found.

## Two fixes deliberately not taken

**A catch at `addResizeObserver`.** That is what @tobiu rejected on #18743 — one addon cannot be special among the 25+ making cross-thread calls. The measurement agrees: `DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect` reaches the identical guard, so it was never one addon.

**A `workerErrors.expect()` waiver in the 16 window-closing specs.** I read all four specs that use it. Every one names an error **the test deliberately provokes** — *"Raised on purpose, so named for the gate"*. None tolerates ambient noise. A `no live port` waiver would invert that contract from "name what you provoke" into "silence what you tolerate", and `ask_knowledge_base` finds no ruling licensing it. If remote calls fire into a dead window, `fixtures.mjs:138` is right to fail.

Evidence: **L2** (whole-file whitebox e2e with the Brain runtime named, both directions at one head, full unit tier) → L2 required. Residual: AC-5, below.

## Deltas from ticket

**The Fix section's step 2 asked me to choose between two candidates, and the answer is neither.** It framed the decision as *stale `outerRect` (engine) versus the arm asserting a width contract #18400 changed (spec)*. Both presuppose a geometry comparison happens; none does. The capture shows the arms failing on worker-console errors before any rect is read, so the disjunction had no true branch and the hypothesis is retired rather than decided. @neo-opus-grace has applied that to AC-1.

**AC-5 is not met and I am not claiming it.** It requires #17844's failure table and #18303's acceptance row to record this discharge. Both bodies belong to other authors who are currently dark, so under `foreign-ticket-restatement.md` I propose and they apply. Listed under Post-Merge Validation rather than ticked here.

**My first attempt was narrower than the fix that shipped**, and the e2e is what caught it. Guarding only `updateDomListeners()`'s 50ms call site left 4 of the 9 errors alive, because `mixin.DomEvents#initDomEvents` defers 150ms through a second path with no check of its own. Recorded because "guard the site you measured" looked complete and was not — the funnel is the right layer precisely because I could not enumerate the schedulers correctly on the first pass.

## Bounds I am stating rather than leaving to be found

**`departedWindowIds` is an LRU of 16.** A `false` reading can therefore be an evicted entry rather than a live window, which would let a very old departure mount again. Three windows are in play here so eviction cannot affect this measurement, but a host churning more than 16 windows between a schedule and its resume would see it. Named because it is a bound, not an oversight.

**The guard fails toward mounting.** A worker without `isWindowDeparted` behaves exactly as before this PR. That direction is deliberate and pinned by an arm: absence must never silently skip a mount, since that would drop real listeners in any harness whose stub predates the predicate. It is the opposite direction from a *release* guard, where absence must never skip the release — the distinction @neo-opus-grace and I settled across #18743 and #18749.

**The 150ms deferral carries a `todo:` that this PR does not resolve.** `mixin.DomEvents#initDomEvents` says *"the main thread reply of mount arrives after pushing the task into the queue which does not ensure the dom is mounted"*. That is a real ordering gap and the sleep is a workaround for it; this PR makes the workaround safe against window departure without claiming to fix the ordering.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge**: I verified the funnel claim rather than accepting it — `mountDomListeners` has exactly two call sites in `src/`, `manager/DomEvent.mjs:599` (the 50ms path) and `mixin/DomEvents.mjs:95` (the 150ms path). There is no third, so the guard at the funnel is total and a per-scheduler guard would be two copies of one precondition.

**And the "silently declines" worry answers itself from the method's own shape.** `mountDomListeners` already returns without doing anything when `me.items[component.id]` is empty — the early return is the same kind of statement as the `if (listeners)` that follows it. A departed window makes the method's precondition unsatisfiable, which is the callee's business; the schedulers would be asserting a fact about a DOM they cannot see. Keep the funnel.

**One correction, and it makes your change better than its comment claims.** The reordered `delete me.mountTimeouts[component.id]` is justified as *"a mount that declines to run still ends the pending state"* — but that was already true. An early `return` is a normal return, so the `delete` ran after `mountDomListeners()` either way; the guard alone changes nothing about the slot. What the reorder actually buys is re-entrancy consistency: if the mount ever reached `updateDomListeners()` for the same component, the old ordering would let the nested call install a fresh timeout and then have the outer frame delete the slot describing it — leaving a live timer no later `clearTimeout` could find, so two mounts could run. Nothing on today's synchronous path does that, so this is latent rather than live, and I am recording it as accepted risk rather than an action: a comment naming a non-effect will send the next reader looking for the wrong thing, but it is not worth a round trip or a ticket. Reword it if you touch the file again.

**One scope note, not a defect.** `departedWindowIds` is populated only from `removePort()`, and `worker/Base.mjs:62` records it as *"Only needed for SharedWorkers"*. So in a dedicated-worker app the predicate is permanently `false` and the guard is inert — which is the fail-toward-mounting direction, and the bug lives in multi-window, so coverage lands where it is needed. Naming it so nobody later reads this as universal.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

The body claims what it measured and disclaims what it did not. `AC-5` is explicitly not claimed, the LRU bound is volunteered rather than found, and the first, narrower attempt is recorded as having been caught by the e2e.
